comment: Training sources for our own detector model (issue #46, MODEL_CONCEPT.md). One entry per source; fetch_sources.py reads this file. 'use': false keeps a sub-source out of the rows. 'terms' is what the original source states, 'terms_source' where it was read (checked 2026-10-11). 'assumed_cc': true marks sub-sources without any licence statement; by project decision of 2026-10-11 they are treated as if under a Creative Commons licence (attribution, share-alike). 'redistribute' says whether the texts may be passed on (published benchmark); false means scripts and row ids only. 'expected' holds the row count and SHA-256 of rows.jsonl that this file produces; fetch_sources.py fails if a run gives something else.

row_format.label: 1 = AI, 0 = human
row_format.group: texts that share a human source document or a prompt; the split keeps a group on one side

hc3.title: HC3 (Human ChatGPT Comparison Corpus)
hc3.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0; a stricter licence of a sub-source takes precedence
notes: Generator: ChatGPT as offered on the web before the paper (arXiv 2301.07597, submitted 2023-01-18). Neither the paper abstract nor the dataset card names a model version, hence 'chatgpt-2022' instead of an API model name.
Human answers in reddit_eli5 have spaces before punctuation (tokenisation artefact of the ELI5 source); texts are stored unchanged, normalise when building the training file.
medicine and finance are marked 'Unknown' by the HC3 authors, who asked the owners. They stay excluded although they have no licence statement (decision of 2026-10-11).

reddit_eli5.terms: HC3 authors' table says 'BSD License', but the ELI5 repository's LICENSE is BSD 'for ELI5 software'; no licence statement for the Reddit texts themselves

open_qa.terms: 'PWC Custom' (HC3 authors' table); Hugging Face tag 'other'

mage.title: MAGE (Deepfake text detection in the wild)
mage.licence: Apache-2.0 (dataset card and GitHub LICENSE; README badge says CC BY 4.0)
notes: In the files label 1 is human and 0 is machine (confirmed in the GitHub README); the rows use our convention (1 = AI).

Generators checked against the paper (arXiv 2305.13242v3, 'Model sets'): 27 models - text-davinci-002/003 and gpt-3.5-turbo; LLaMA 6B/13B/30B/65B (the files call the smallest '7B'); GLM-130B; FLAN-T5 small to xxl; OPT 125M to 30B and OPT-IML; T0-3B/11B and BLOOM-7B1; GPT-J-6B and GPT-NeoX-20B. The unseen-domain set is 'GPT-4' without a version.
Prompt types: 'continuation' gives the model the first 30 words of the human text; 'topical' and 'specified' (OpenAI models only) give a topic, the latter with the kind of source.

The paraphrase set was made with gpt-3.5-turbo, sentence by sentence, from human and GPT-4 texts; MAGE counts all of it as machine (paper and README). The human rows of that file repeat those of test_ood_set_gpt.csv (762 of 762) and are skipped.

No document ids. For train/valid/test the group is a hash of the first 12 words: that links 96% of the 'continuation' texts in train.csv to their human text. 'topical' and 'specified' texts cannot be linked.

The two out-of-domain files have no usable link between a text and its paraphrase (the opening changes, the rows are not aligned). All their rows of one sub-source therefore share one group (mage:ood:<sub-source>), so that a text and its paraphrase never end up on different sides.
Because of the shared opening, the first 30 words of a 'continuation' text are human-written. Short excerpts must not be cut from the start of these rows.
MAGE's own train/valid/test split is not by document (about 7% of valid and test openings also occur in train); it is kept in meta.split only.

eli5.terms: repository LICENSE is BSD 'for ELI5 software'; Hugging Face tag 'unknown'

wp.terms: no licence statement for the data (fairseq code is MIT)

roct.terms: no licence; access by form, 'free to everyone'

hswag.human_source: HellaSwag (Zellers et al. 2019): ActivityNet captions and wikiHow
hswag.terms: wikiHow text is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0; the HellaSwag repository is blocked on GitHub since 2026-09-14 after a copyright notice by wikiHow
hswag.reason: non-commercial terms and a takedown by the rights holder

sci_gen.terms: no licence statement found (paper announces a public release)

tldr.terms: no licence statement on the dataset card

xsum.terms: repository LICENSE is MIT (code); Hugging Face tag 'unknown'; articles are BBC copyright
xsum.reason: BBC articles: left out like raid/news, although this dataset states no terms of its own (decision of 2026-10-11)

yelp.terms: Yelp dataset terms: academic, non-commercial; Hugging Face tag 'other'

cnn.terms: Apache-2.0 (Hugging Face card), MIT (repository). The articles are publisher copyright; used on the basis of the stated dataset licence, texts not redistributed (decision of 2026-10-11)

imdb.terms: no licence stated, only a citation request; Hugging Face tag 'other'

raid.title: RAID

not_fetched.test.csv: unlabelled (hidden test set of the RAID leaderboard)
not_fetched.extra.csv: code, Czech and German; not needed for the English version

notes: train.csv has 5,615,820 rows: 467,985 without attack and the same rows under 11 adversarial attacks. 'attacks' selects which ones become rows; the group links an attacked text to its original.
Every human document has 34 generations (11 models, 2 or 4 decoding settings each), so label 1 outweighs label 0 by 34:1.

Generators checked against the paper (arXiv 2405.07940, table 10): gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, gpt-4-0613, text-davinci-002, gpt2-xl, Llama-2-70b-chat-hf, Mistral-7B-v0.1, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1, mpt-30b, mpt-30b-chat, Cohere command via generate() and via chat().

Dates: the paper says most human documents are from datasets before 2022 and that only Wikipedia and Abstracts include later documents. A sample of 8 human abstracts from train.csv looked up on arXiv was published 2013 to 2021.

abstracts.human_source: arXiv abstracts (Paul and Rakshit 2021, Kaggle 'arXiv Paper Abstracts')

books.human_source: CMU Book Summary Dataset (Bamman and Smith 2013), Wikipedia plot summaries

news.terms: 'for non-commercial and research purposes only'; articles are BBC copyright

poetry.terms: CC0 according to the Kaggle uploader; the poems' own copyright is not addressed

recipes.terms: agreement with Poznan University of Technology: 'only for non-commercial research and educational purposes'

reddit.terms: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo record 1043504, Hugging Face card)

reviews.terms: no licence stated, only a citation request; Hugging Face tag 'other'

wiki.terms: 'cc' (dataset card); Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA
